text:
lina: quick thread  saw higher-than-expected tail latency on safetensors-small-shard workloads. suspicion: lots of tiny reads -> nvme queue thrash. exploring a coalescer that merges adjacent chunk reads into larger sequential IO.

omar: nice. does coalescing risk reading too much memory for eviction-constrained nodes?

lina: tradeoff. plan is adaptive coalesce: only merge if merged_size <= budget_remaining_for_request. budget is per-request warmup currency, deducted as we issue merged reads.

frank: how do we compute budget? per-tenant rate limit? per-route?

lina: two-layer budget: global per-worker token pool (bytes/sec) + per-tenant burst tokens. tenant tokens cap how many bytes a tenant can warmup concurrently.

frank: that sounds reasonable. need to ensure shared-cache correctness: merged read may prefetch bytes that belong to other shards; are we ok with cross-shard reads?

lina: we only merge adjacent ranges within the same checkpoint file. we won't cross manifest boundaries. for sharded checkpoints the coalescer gets a `shard_id` hint.

tlewis: can we rely on safetensors index for adjacency? what about gzipped bundles where adjacency doesn't map to file offsets?

omar: gzipped bundles break range reads. coalescer should detect compressed transport and disable merge, fallback to existing small-range reads.

lina: agreed. heuristic: if transport supports HTTP range and `x-checkpoint-compressed: false` then enable coalesce. else off. Also add `x-coalesce-enabled: true|false` header so Private installs can opt-out.

frank: telemetry needed: `coalesce_hits`, `coalesce_bytes`, `coalesce_disabled_reason`. ops needs per-tenant charts.

lina: yup. also tracking `warmup_budget_remaining` per-request sample.

tlewis: how about correctness when a merged read returns partial data because of network errors? rollback semantics?

lina: transport returns a status for the merged op. we map to individual range failures and allow retry per-range. we also implement a small atomicity window: if merged read partially fails, mark merged region as degraded and fall back to single-range retries for those subranges.

omar: testing plan: 1) unit tests for merge heuristics; 2) single-host replay with pathological tiny-range workloads; 3) cluster canary with 10% traffic; 4) verify 95p latency and warmup bytes.

frank: perf simulation: i'll run a synthetic sweep varying shard-size distribution and tenant-burst budgets. want result by EOW.

infra-bot: deploy-notice: feature-flagged coalescer branch deployed to canary-1 by tlewis at 2026-03-21T16:10:00Z

tlewis: rollout notes: feature default false; enable via `runtime.coalesce.enable=true` on canary. please avoid enabling on private clusters until RFC approved.

lina: RFC items: API change to `ReadHint` to include `shard_id` and `checkpoint_compressed` and `coalesce_preference`. need small transport codec bump. i'll draft RFC and own it.

omar: concern: merged reads could increase memory pressure on background eviction. maybe add an estimate to admission: `merged_read_memory_estimate = merged_size + read_buffer_overhead`. if node memory saturating, reduce coalesce aggressiveness.

frank: good call. add backoff policy: coalesce_factor *= 0.5 when mem_pressure > 85%. slowly recover.

lina: noted. also add safety: never coalesce above 4MB default unless tenant has high burst allowance.

tlewis: ownership: lina RFC + PR, frank runs sims, omar does transport changes, i'll manage canary rollout and dashboards.

omar: one last nit: make sure index-first loaders that emit small-range manifests include an `adjacency_hint` to help coalescer pick safe merge boundaries.

lina: will add to RFC. thanks team :rocket:
